🚨 BREAKING NEWS: An Open Secret:
Pedophilia in Hollywood

An Open Secret investigates allegations of sexual abuse and exploitation of children and young performers within the entertainment industry, drawing upon testimony from survivors and examining the environments and networks that allegedly allowed predators to gain access to vulnerable young people.

What makes the documentary especially disturbing is not simply the individual allegations it presents, but the broader questions it raises about institutional protection, silence, professional retaliation, and the enormous imbalance of power between young performers and the adults capable of determining their careers.

For years, the entertainment industry has faced accusations that abusive behavior was known about, whispered about, joked about, or treated as an "open secret" long before the wider public became aware of it.

And that is precisely why this documentary deserves attention.

It should not require believing that everyone in Hollywood is involved, nor should unproven allegations automatically be treated as established fact. The documented testimony of survivors is horrifying enough without exaggeration.

The important question is how predators can operate within powerful institutions while people around them fail to intervene, look the other way, fear professional consequences, or prioritize reputations and careers over vulnerable human beings.

Yet despite the gravity of its subject matter, most people I speak with have never even heard of this documentary.

That needs to change.

Watch it. Investigate the claims for yourself. Examine the evidence. Listen to the survivors. Distinguish what has been documented from what remains alleged.

Because when children are being exploited, protecting powerful institutions should never matter more than discovering the Truth.

How many people knew what was happening and chose to remain silent?

How many warnings were ignored because exposing the truth might have threatened careers, reputations, money, or powerful institutions?

How does an alleged predator continue gaining access to vulnerable young people when others within the same industry have already raised concerns?

What systems failed the survivors, and who had the responsibility and authority to intervene?

Why are survivors so often terrified of speaking publicly about powerful people and institutions?

How many victims never came forward at all because they believed nobody would listen, nobody would believe them, or speaking out would destroy their future?

Which allegations have been independently corroborated, which resulted in criminal or civil proceedings, and which remain unproven?

What happened to the people accused in the documentary after these allegations became public?

What protections have actually been implemented for child performers since then, and are those protections enough?

Why had So Many people Never even
Heard of this Documentary?

And perhaps the most important question of all: if credible evidence of abuse exists, why should wealth, celebrity, institutional influence, or professional power ever stand between a child and justice?

We should not need conspiracy theories or sensationalism to recognize the seriousness of child exploitation. Follow the evidence. Listen to survivors. Demand accountability where the facts support it. Protect children before reputations, careers, corporations, political interests, or institutions.

THIS NEEDS TO STOP.

PLEASE WAKE UP, GUYS.

⚠️ Bitcoin mining divide pushes Luke Dashjr out of OCEAN 

📣 OCEAN co-founder Luke Dashjr left the Bitcoin mining pool on Aug. 29 after reaching a mutual separation agreement with its parent company, Mummolin Inc. He resigned as chairman, chief technology officer and director. OCEAN and Dashjr attributed the separation to “different visions for the future of Bitcoin mining following the recent protocol developments.” The statement did not identify the developments or explain the areas of disagreement.

📊 The wording therefore does not confirm whether a single Bitcoin protocol proposal caused the split. Dashjr has participated in public debates about transaction policies, mining decentralization and alternative Bitcoin software. Connecting the departure to any particular dispute would require further confirmation from the parties. Dashjr had already stepped back from his OCEAN responsibilities earlier in August. His permanent departure now removes him from the company’s leadership and ownership structure.

🌐 The company did not announce a replacement chairman or chief technology officer. It also provided no details about how Dashjr’s former technical responsibilities will be distributed. Dashjr plans to create a new venture called CONVOY. The joint statement said the project would continue his mission of decentralizing Bitcoin mining.

Before sunrise, satellite images suggested that Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline had been hit. Six fire hotspots appeared near the route from Abqaiq to Yanbu. Saudi Arabia has not confirmed an attack or damage to the line. 

The pipeline carries up to 7 million barrels a day. It exists for one job: keep Saudi crude moving when Hormuz becomes a shooting gallery.

The market saw the images and paid attention. Brent moved from about $96 to more than $106 on Thursday. It briefly approached $110 on Friday. 

It then fell more than 3% to roughly $104 after reports that Gulf states and Iran were working on a temporary arrangement for shipping through Hormuz.

That is the regional business model now. A smoke plume adds billions to the oil bill. A rumor of an Omani corridor gives part of it back. The pipeline may be damaged. The fear premium is already pumping at full capacity.

Qatar offers the crueler version. Its LNG exports have reportedly collapsed by 96% after an Iranian strike damaged the Ras Laffan complex. 

The country that built the world’s largest LNG export operation is now reportedly negotiating long-term U.S. gas purchases. Repairs may take up to five years. Qatar spent decades selling the world gas. The war turned it into a customer with better branding.

The consequences do not stop at the Gulf. Higher energy costs feed into freight, food and consumer prices. Eilat loses traffic when Red Sea shipping becomes a target range. Egypt loses transit revenue when vessels avoid the Suez route.

Hormuz was supposed to be the vulnerable route. Yanbu was supposed to be the workaround. The Houthis may have turned both into financial instruments.
